text:
emma: Heads-up — JonesCorp opened a ticket: their Private control plane mTLS started failing after a firewall update at ~09:40 PT. They see ClientHello but no ServerHello, connection eventually times out. Ticket #J-4921.

support-bot: ticket J-4921 created, severity P1 assigned. Attachments: tcpdump, client logs.

emma: Quick summary from customer:
- Symptoms: client TLS handshake stalls at ClientHello (no ServerHello)
- Affected from two egress IPs only (10.44.22.11/32 and 10.44.22.12/32 NATed on their ASA)
- Works if they bounces traffic through corp VPN -> our control plane works.

raj: Can you paste the tcpdump snippet? look for retransmits / icmp port unreachable / RSTs.

emma: Pasting a small tcpdump slice they sent:
```
14:02:11.123456 IP 10.44.22.11.54321 > cp.redwood.com.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
14:02:11.124120 IP 10.44.22.11.54321 > cp.redwood.com.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 0, win 64240, length 511
14:02:11.124200 IP 10.44.22.11.54322 > cp.redwood.com.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 0, win 64240, length 511  # second simultaneous flow
14:02:21.124500 IP 10.44.22.11.54321 > cp.redwood.com.443: Flags [P.], seq 512:1024, ack 0, win 64240, length 512  # retransmit observed
```

marta: That first pattern (S then pushed data) looks like they send ClientHello in same TCP segment (ok). Retransmit at +10s suggests server didn't ACK. Could be server never saw packets or reply path broken.

leo: Any ICMP unreachable or firewall logs from their ASA? They mentioned a firewall change earlier.

emma: Customer says they flipped an egress macro that normalizes SNI to empty for compliance. They denied it would affect TLS but maybe a proxy rewrite is running. They also gave this iptables-like rule from their egress box: `-j MARK --set-mark 0x1` and a NAT map.

raj: If SNI gets stripped or replaced, some middleboxes drop TLS ClientHello if they expect valid SNI. But more likely asymmetric routing/NAT rewriting causes server's SYN-ACK/ServerHello to be routed to a different firewall path and dropped. Ask for a packet capture on our side (server) to confirm if we see the incoming ClientHello.

emma: Customer ran `sudo tcpdump -n -i ens5 host 10.44.22.11 and port 443` toward our control plane and report: they DO NOT see any inbound packets arriving at their NAT public IP from cp.redwood.com.

marta: That suggests server-side responses never reach their egress NAT. Could be our replies hitting an intermediate firewall that blocks by destination port or state. We need our packet capture on the control plane instance that handled the SYN.

deploy-bot: deploy-log: control-plane instance cp-0123 processed connection from 54.213.81.92:443 at 14:02:11 UTC (log id cp/conn/2026-06-11/14:02/0123).

raj: Emma — can you request a pcap around that timestamp on our cp host? If we see ServerHello out, then it's definitely dropped on return path. If we don't see ClientHello at all, maybe ISP/NAT is rewriting source or blackholing.

emma: Done — I'm attaching our pcap excerpt from cp-0123: we see the SYN, but we do NOT see the subsequent ClientHello payload from 10.44.22.11 — only the TCP SYN and then a RST from an intermediate device (10.200.5.1) 2s later.

leo: RST from 10.200.5.1 — that's likely their egress proxy or an ISP middlebox. What does traceroute/tcptraceroute show to cp.redwood.com from their egress IPs?

emma: Customer ran `tcptraceroute cp.redwood.com 443` and shows hop 6 stalls then a TTL exceeded returning from 10.200.5.1.

raj: Two parallel possibilities: 1) Their proxy is doing deep packet inspection and dropping TLS when SNI is blank/forbidden. 2) Asymmetric NAT causes server replies to take a different egress that doesn't have an established state so firewall RSTs. Both consistent with RST from 10.200.5.1.

marta: Workaround idea: ask them to add egress allowlist for control-plane IPs (we'll provide our access IPs and ASNs) and to disable the SNI-normalization rule for traffic to cp.redwood.com. Also ask them to preserve source port for these flows (avoid port randomization on NAT) and disable any TCP MSS/segmentation rewriting for that host.

emma: Sent step list to customer: 1) temp allowlist cp IPs + ASNs; 2) disable SNI rewrite for cp.redwood.com; 3) capture full pcap on egress device; 4) confirm NAT preserves source port.

support-bot: Update: customer will test allowlist and SNI rule removal in a maintenance window at 23:00 local. They want us on standby.

leo: We'll plan to watch logs. If allowlist/disable SNI fixes it, root cause = egress inspection/proxy. If not, escalate to network infra for BGP/ASN path check.

emma: Customer reports back after test: removing SNI rewrite fixed handshake immediately. They confirmed ServerHello seen and mutual TLS completed.

raj: Great — root cause confirmed: egress proxy was stripping SNI and then inline DPI blocked the TLS flow; because the proxy also manipulated NAT, return packets were hitting a device that reset the connection.

marta: Please ask them to keep allowlist in place for our control plane IPs and roll a config change to exclude cp.redwood.com from the SNI-normalization rule. Also recommend they run the following check to avoid regressions:
```
# quick check from their egress box
openssl s_client -connect cp.redwood.com:443 -servername cp.redwood.com -tlsextdebug -status
```

emma: I'll close the ticket with root cause, repro steps, and preventative recommendations. Marking as resolved after customer CI confirms permanent fix. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: ticket J-4921 status -> resolved (customer confirmed).
